packages.name: cors
packages.synopsis: Package cors is net/http handler to handle CORS related requests as defined by http://www.w3.org/TR/cors/
packages.doc:
Package cors is net/http handler to handle CORS related requests
as defined by http://www.w3.org/TR/cors/

You can configure it by passing an option struct to cors.New:

	c := cors.New(cors.Options{
	    AllowedOrigins:   []string{"foo.com"},
	    AllowedMethods:   []string{http.MethodGet, http.MethodPost, http.MethodDelete},
	    AllowCredentials: true,
	})

Then insert the handler in the chain:

	handler = c.Handler(handler)

See Options documentation for more options.

The resulting handler is a standard net/http handler.

funcs.name: AllowAll
funcs.doc:
AllowAll create a new Cors handler with permissive configuration allowing all
origins with all standard methods with any header and credentials.

funcs.name: Default
funcs.doc: Default creates a new Cors handler with default options.

funcs.name: New
funcs.doc: New creates a new Cors handler with the provided options.

types.name: Cors

methods.name: Handler
methods.doc:
Handler apply the CORS specification on the request, and add relevant CORS headers
as necessary.

methods.name: OriginAllowed
methods.doc: check the Origin of a request. No origin at all is also allowed.

methods.name: ServeHTTP
methods.signature: func  ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, next http.HandlerFunc)

types.name: Options
types.doc: Options is a configuration container to setup the CORS middleware.

fields.name: AllowedOrigins
fields.doc:
AllowedOrigins is a list of origins a cross-domain request can be executed from.
If the special "*" value is present in the list, all origins will be allowed.
An origin may contain a wildcard (*) to replace 0 or more characters
(i.e.: http://*.domain.com). Usage of wildcards implies a small performance penalty.
Only one wildcard can be used per origin.
Default value is ["*"]

fields.name: AllowOriginFunc
fields.doc:
AllowOriginFunc is a custom function to validate the origin. It take the
origin as argument and returns true if allowed or false otherwise. If
this option is set, the content of `AllowedOrigins` is ignored.

fields.name: AllowOriginRequestFunc
fields.doc:
AllowOriginRequestFunc is a custom function to validate the origin. It
takes the HTTP Request object and the origin as argument and returns true
if allowed or false otherwise. If headers are used take the decision,
consider using AllowOriginVaryRequestFunc instead. If this option is set,
the contents of `AllowedOrigins`, `AllowOriginFunc` are ignored.

Deprecated: use `AllowOriginVaryRequestFunc` instead.

fields.name: AllowOriginVaryRequestFunc
fields.doc:
AllowOriginVaryRequestFunc is a custom function to validate the origin.
It takes the HTTP Request object and the origin as argument and returns
true if allowed or false otherwise with a list of headers used to take
that decision if any so they can be added to the Vary header. If this
option is set, the contents of `AllowedOrigins`, `AllowOriginFunc` and
`AllowOriginRequestFunc` are ignored.

fields.name: AllowedMethods
fields.doc:
AllowedMethods is a list of methods the client is allowed to use with
cross-domain requests. Default value is simple methods (HEAD, GET and POST).

fields.name: AllowedHeaders
fields.doc:
AllowedHeaders is list of non simple headers the client is allowed to use with
cross-domain requests.
If the special "*" value is present in the list, all headers will be allowed.
Default value is [].

fields.name: ExposedHeaders
fields.doc:
ExposedHeaders indicates which headers are safe to expose to the API of a CORS
API specification

fields.name: MaxAge
fields.doc:
MaxAge indicates how long (in seconds) the results of a preflight request
can be cached. Default value is 0, which stands for no
Access-Control-Max-Age header to be sent back, resulting in browsers
using their default value (5s by spec). If you need to force a 0 max-age,
set `MaxAge` to a negative value (ie: -1).

fields.name: AllowCredentials
fields.doc:
AllowCredentials indicates whether the request can include user credentials like
cookies, HTTP authentication or client side SSL certificates.

fields.name: AllowPrivateNetwork
fields.doc:
AllowPrivateNetwork indicates whether to accept cross-origin requests over a
private network.

fields.name: OptionsPassthrough
fields.doc:
OptionsPassthrough instructs preflight to let other potential next handlers to
process the OPTIONS method. Turn this on if your application handles OPTIONS.

fields.name: OptionsSuccessStatus
fields.doc:
Provides a status code to use for successful OPTIONS requests.
Default value is http.StatusNoContent (204).

fields.name: Debug
fields.doc: Debugging flag adds additional output to debug server side CORS issues

fields.name: Logger
fields.doc: Adds a custom logger, implies Debug is true
